Babe. That's my dad. You're my... colleague. From church.
{tell}

yahoo.text: The MC jokes: 'All yahoo boys, EFCC is at the gate!' Everybody laughs. Kayode is already behind a canopy.

gambler.text: The man's first words: 'Where is the watch I gave you?' Kayode: 'Servicing, sir.'

trust_fund.text: He shows you his screen: 14 missed calls from 'Daddy'. Daddy is now ten feet away.

choices.label: Play along. Colleague. From church.
choices.receipt: You pretended to be his colleague from church.

outcomes.text: You shake the man's hand like a deacon. Kayode relaxes for the first time all day.

trust_fund.text: His father squints. 'Colleague. Hm.' Retired judge. He knows a lie. He also lets it slide.

choices.label: Introduce yourself properly: "I'm the one he's dating."
choices.receipt: You introduced yourself honestly to his father.

outcomes.text: The man laughs, a real one. 'Finally, somebody with sense.'
Silence. Kayode says nothing. His father says nothing. The jollof says nothing.

yahoo.text: The man is not his father. It's 'Uncle Bright', who pays him monthly. Uncle Bright looks at you like fresh stock.

gambler.text: His father: 'Then tell him to pay back his sister's ₦2m.' Silence. Then jollof.

trust_fund.text: Justice Ogunleye (rtd) shakes your hand. 'Honest. Good. He needs that.' Kayode nearly faints, then grins all evening.

choices.label: Spray him. Make the videographer happy.
choices.receipt: You sprayed money at his cousin's wedding.

outcomes.text: The videographer worships you. You're on every aunty's WhatsApp status by sunset.

choices.label: Spray crisp ₦500s. Slowly. Strategically.
choices.receipt: You sprayed ₦500 notes, slowly.

outcomes.text: From far away it looks like serious money. The aunties approve of your mathematics.

choices.label: Find cousin Tunde. He always knows.
choices.receipt: You asked cousin Tunde for the gist.

outcomes.text: Tunde, three Smirnoffs deep: 'Kay? Good guy. Too scared of his papa.'

yahoo.text: Tunde, drunk: 'Kay's clients are all in America. All women. All lonely.' He laughs. You don't.

gambler.text: Tunde: 'He owes me ₦800k. And Dapo. And his sister. Don't lend him anything, I beg.'

trust_fund.text: Tunde: 'His dad cut his older brother off for one arrest. Kay's been running ever since.' It suddenly makes sense.

choices.label: "Sir, I've heard all about Sunday lunch."
choices.receipt: You told his father you'd heard about Sunday lunch.

outcomes.text: The man blinks. 'Has he? Hm.' Kayode looks at you like you just passed an exam.

yahoo.text: 'Sunday lunch? With me? I haven't seen this boy on a Sunday since 2021.' Interesting.

gambler.text: 'Sunday lunch? He comes to borrow, not to eat.' Kayode laughs too loud.

trust_fund.text: His father softens. 'He told you about Sunday? He never tells anyone anything.'

beats.text: 6am. Hammering on his door. Navy jackets with yellow letters.
We're looking for Kayode Ogunleye. Also known as Gregory. Also known as Captain Mark.
Babe, hide the laptop. Please. Please.
{tell}

yahoo.text: The officer holds up a printout: your face, lifted from Kayode's Instagram, beside a fake pilot profile.

choices.label: Hide the laptop in your bag.
choices.receipt: You hid his laptop from EFCC.

outcomes.text: They don't search you. He kisses you like you saved his life. You probably did. That's the problem.
They search your bag first. 'You're coming with us too.'

choices.label: Tell the officers everything you know.
choices.receipt: You told EFCC everything you knew.

outcomes.text: You talk for an hour. 'You're a witness, not a suspect. Keep your phone on.' Kayode can't look at you.

choices.label: "Get a lawyer. I'm not going anywhere."
choices.receipt: You stood by him during the EFCC raid.

outcomes.text: They take him for questioning. He calls from Ikoyi office: 'Nobody has ever stayed.' You're either loyal or mad. Possibly both.

choices.label: Walk out past the officers. Block him in the lift.
choices.receipt: You walked out and blocked him in the lift.

outcomes.text: You don't look back. In the lift you delete 300 photos and one future.

choices.label: Go live: "EFCC is at Gregory's house."
choices.receipt: You livestreamed his EFCC arrest.

outcomes.text: 40,000 viewers. The officers wave. Kayode hides his face behind a throw pillow that says LIVE LAUGH LOVE.

choices.label: "My account was in this. Am I on your list?"
choices.receipt: You asked EFCC if your account was on their list.

outcomes.text: The officer checks. Your account number is there. 'Come to the Ikoyi office Monday. Bring a lawyer.'

choices.label: Hand over your Gregory screenshots.
choices.receipt: You handed EFCC your screenshots.

outcomes.text: The officer smiles for the first time. 'You've done our job for us.' Kayode looks at you like a stranger.

choices.label: Stick to the story: "We met in church."
choices.receipt: You told EFCC you met in church.

outcomes.text: 'Which church?' You both answer at the same time. Different churches. Different denominations.

beats.text: Midnight. A man in a football jersey is on Kayode's couch, eating Kayode's suya.
Kayode owes ₦9m since Tuesday. Today is Friday. Is it you that will pay?
Babe, it's a misunderstanding. Crypto will pump by Monday.
{tell}

gambler.text: Kunle is wearing a gold Rolex. Kayode's Rolex. 'Servicing,' indeed.

choices.label: Pay ₦100k to buy him a week.
choices.broke_text: Kunle laughs at your balance. Then asks for your mum's number.
choices.receipt: You paid his bookie to buy him a week.

outcomes.text: Kunle counts it and eats another suya. 'One week.' Kayode swears it was his last bet. It wasn't even his last bet today.

choices.label: "You need help, not money. I'll come with you."
choices.receipt: You told him he needs help, and offered to go with him.

outcomes.text: He cries, properly. Then deletes four apps in front of you and hands you his card. 'Keep it. I can't be trusted with it.'

choices.label: Pack your bag. Leave them to it.
choices.receipt: You packed your bag and left.

outcomes.text: You leave Kunle and Kayode arguing about Arsenal's back four. Somebody had to leave first.

choices.label: Go live: "Lekki Big Boy owes ₦9m."
choices.receipt: You livestreamed his gambling debt.

outcomes.text: The Parlour crashes. Kunle waves at the camera, advertising. Kayode's crypto group chat leaves him on read.

choices.label: "I bet with you too. I'm part of this."
choices.receipt: You admitted you'd gambled with him too.

outcomes.text: He laughs and cries at the same time. 'You're the only one who ever bet with me and stayed.' You both swear off. Together.

choices.label: "Where's my ₦50k that you 'doubled'?"
choices.receipt: You asked where your 'doubled' ₦50k went.

outcomes.text: Kunle answers for him: 'Your ₦50k? Galatasaray. Second half. Lost.'

choices.label: Call cousin Tunde to come and help.
choices.receipt: You called his cousin Tunde to help.

outcomes.text: Tunde arrives in boxers with ₦300k and a cousin's fury. 'Kay. This is the last time.' Kunle leaves with half. Kayode cries into Tunde's shoulder.

choices.label: [Corporate] Restructure his debt on a spreadsheet.
choices.receipt: You built a repayment plan for his gambling debt.

outcomes.text: By 3am there's a nine-month repayment plan with formulas. Kunle is impressed. Kayode is in love.

beats.text: Lunch in Ikoyi. His father, a retired judge, orders water and studies you like a case file.
My son runs at every siren because I said one arrest and he is cut off. Tell me honestly. Is he in trouble?
{tell}

trust_fund.text: Beside you, Kayode is blinking very fast. 'Allergies,' he says. To his father.

choices.label: Tell the truth: he's soft, not criminal.
choices.receipt: You told his father the truth: he's soft, not criminal.

outcomes.text: The judge is quiet a long time. 'Soft. His mother was soft.' He pays the bill. Kayode looks at you like you raised the dead.

choices.label: "With respect, sir, your rules made him run."
choices.receipt: You told a retired judge his rules made his son run.

outcomes.text: One eyebrow rises. Then he laughs, once. 'Finally, someone argues back.'
'Young person, I have jailed better speakers.' Kayode kicks you under the table. Softly. Lovingly.

choices.label: "Sir, is the allowance negotiable for two?"
choices.receipt: You asked a retired judge about the allowance.

outcomes.text: He chokes on his water. Then, to Kayode: 'This one is bold. Your mother was bold.'
'So you're here for the money.' Kayode spends the rest of lunch apologising to two people.

choices.label: Post a selfie with the judge. Caption it.
choices.receipt: You posted a selfie with his father.

outcomes.text: 'With the in-laws ⚖️' goes viral. The judge's grandchildren see it. The judge sees it. Kayode sees nothing; he's left.

choices.label: "I ran with him once. He was scared, not guilty."
choices.receipt: You told his father you ran with him from a raid.

outcomes.text: The judge looks at his son a long time. 'You ran because of me.' First time Kayode has seen him look sorry.

choices.label: "He cries at Nollywood films, sir. He's harmless."
choices.receipt: You told his father he cries at Nollywood films.

outcomes.text: Kayode: 'Betrayal.' The judge, smiling for the first time: 'His mother did too.'

choices.label: Give the judge white lilies. "For her."
choices.receipt: You brought white lilies for his late mother.

outcomes.text: The old man holds them for a long time. 'He told you about his mother.' He nods at Kayode. 'Keep this one.'

choices.label: "We met in church, sir."
choices.receipt: You told the judge you met in church.

outcomes.text: 'Did you.' Not a question. A verdict. Kayode confesses everything in four minutes. The judge almost smiles.

beats.text: A DM from a stranger with no profile picture.
That guy in your video. Benz, waves, gold chain. Where do you know him from?

choices.label: "He's my man. Problem?"
choices.receipt: You told a stranger he's your man.

outcomes.text: Seen. No reply. Somehow that's worse.

yahoo.text: 'Tell Gregory my aunty in Houston wants her $8,000 back.' Receipts follow. Lots of receipts.

gambler.text: 'Tell him Kunle Odds is looking for him. Nice location tag, by the way.'

trust_fund.text: 'Tell him his father's driver saw your video. Good luck to you both.'

choices.label: Delete the video. Block the stranger.
choices.receipt: You deleted the video and blocked the stranger.

outcomes.text: Deleted. Somebody screenshotted it first. Somebody always does.

choices.label: "Why? Who's asking?"
choices.receipt: You asked the stranger who was asking.

outcomes.text: No reply. The account disappears an hour later.

yahoo.text: 'A lawyer. For a woman in Ohio.' Then the chat is deleted from her side.

gambler.text: 'Someone he owes. Tell him Friday is the deadline.'

trust_fund.text: 'His sister. Daddy saw it. And Daddy is smiling, for once. Don't tell Kay I said that.'

choices.label: Forward it to Kayode: "Who is this?"
choices.receipt: You forwarded the stranger's DM to him.

outcomes.text: He calls immediately. 'Ignore it.' You can't.

yahoo.text: He calls in a panic: 'Delete it. Delete everything with my face.' You hear him deleting his own Instagram.

gambler.text: 'Ignore it. Small debt.' He says 'small' the way Lagos says 'small traffic'.

trust_fund.text: He laughs, then groans. 'My sister. So Daddy knows about you now. Brace.'

beats.text: About the other night. I know how it looked. I can't explain on the phone. Can I see you? Please.

choices.label: "Come and explain in person."
choices.receipt: You let him come and explain the raid.

outcomes.text: He comes with flowers and a story. You listen.

yahoo.text: He comes with flowers and a story about 'a misunderstanding with a client'. By dessert there are three versions.

gambler.text: He comes with flowers and asks, casually, if the lounge ever chased the tab. His eyes say he owes them too.

trust_fund.text: He sits on your bed and tells you everything: his father, his brother, the one-arrest rule. Then he cries. Then he denies it.

choices.label: Block him for 24 hours. Let him sweat.
choices.receipt: You blocked him for a day after the raid.

outcomes.text: He sends 41 messages through your Bestie. She forwards all of them, with commentary.

choices.label: "Send me something for my trauma."
choices.receipt: You asked him to pay for your trauma.

outcomes.text: ₦100k in ten seconds. 'Sorry is not enough. Here is more sorry.'
'Of course, babe!' Nothing arrives. 'Network.' Lagos network never fails like this for incoming.

yahoo.text: ₦200k lands from an account named 'Barbara Jenkins'. You stare at the name for a long time.

trust_fund.text: ₦150k and a four-paragraph essay. Paragraph three is just 'I'm sorry' eleven times.

choices.label: "You left me there, Kayode. Alone."
choices.receipt: You told him he abandoned you at the raid.

outcomes.text: Long silence. 'I know. I'll spend the rest of the week making it up to you.' He does. Mostly.

gambler.text: 'I know. I panicked. I owe that lounge money too.' Too.

choices.label: "We survived together. Dinner's on you."
choices.receipt: You told him you survived the raid together.

outcomes.text: He books the rooftop in Ikoyi and orders exactly what you had the first night. He remembered.

beats.text: Babe, about your ₦50k 😅 Good news and bad news. Which one first?

choices.label: "Good news first."
choices.receipt: You asked for the good news first.

outcomes.text: 'Here's your ₦50k back.' That's it. That was the good news.

yahoo.text: '₦100k, as promised!' The sender name is 'Mrs Linda Hoffmann'. He won't explain the bad news.

gambler.text: 'Good news: I nearly won. Bad news: nearly.' Your ₦50k died on a Turkish second-division match.

trust_fund.text: 'Good news: here's ₦100k. Bad news: Daddy found out I borrowed and lectured me for an hour. Worth it.'

choices.label: "Bad news first. I'm Lagos-strong."
choices.receipt: You asked for the bad news first.

outcomes.text: 'Bad news: it took longer than I said.' ₦50k lands. No interest. No shame.

yahoo.text: 'Bad news: the client is processing.' ₦60k lands from a stranger's account. 'Good news: here's something.'

gambler.text: 'Bad news: it's gone. Good news: I have a new sure one. Send ₦50k more?'

trust_fund.text: 'Bad news: I'm terrible at business. Good news: I paid you back from my allowance, with interest.'

choices.label: "Keep the news. Send my money."
choices.receipt: You told him to skip the news and send your money.

outcomes.text: ₦50k lands. No emoji. Respectful, but cold.

gambler.text: 'Give me till Friday.' Friday has been booked since 2019.

beats.text: 1am. Dapo slides into your DMs.
You and Kay are not serious. Come and see Ikoyi from a G-Wagon. Tonight.

choices.label: Go. One ride.
choices.receipt: You took a night ride with his rival.

outcomes.text: One ride becomes a night drive down Lekki-Epe and back. Dapo talks about himself for two hours. Your Bestie loves the gist.
Tunde sees you in the G-Wagon at a red light. By sunrise, Kayode has the photo.

choices.label: Screenshot it to Kayode.
choices.receipt: You showed him his rival's DM.

outcomes.text: Kayode calls Dapo. You hear the shouting from your side of Lekki. Then: 'Thank you for telling me.'

gambler.text: Kayode: 'Dapo? I'll beat him at FIFA for ₦500k.' Of course he will. Of course it's a bet.

choices.label: Leave Dapo on read. Forever.
choices.receipt: You left his rival on read.

outcomes.text: He sends a sad emoji, then a voice note of himself singing. Badly. You screenshot it for the group chat.

beats.text: You went through my phone. I said don't. So go on. What did you find?

choices.label: "I'm sorry. I got scared."
choices.receipt: You apologised for going through his phone.

outcomes.text: He's quiet. 'Next time ask me. I might even answer.'

trust_fund.text: 'Scared of what? Daddy's texts?' He laughs, a little hurt. 'Ask me anything. Just ask.'

choices.label: "Enough to have questions. Answer them."
choices.receipt: You demanded answers after snooping.

outcomes.text: He answers some. You believe some.

yahoo.text: An hour on 'foreign clients'. Not one sentence is true. Every one of them is smooth.

gambler.text: He admits the betting. 'Like, ten percent of what you think.' It's ninety.

trust_fund.text: He answers everything. Daddy, the allowance, the note about you. You feel stupid and loved.

choices.label: "And I'll check again if I need to."
choices.receipt: You told him you'd snoop again.

outcomes.text: He changes his passcode in front of you. Then again. Then he sleeps in the other room.

beats.text: Babe, I'm tired of these Ikoyi restaurants. Real talk? Give me amala in Ojuelegba any day. ₦3,500 and I'm a happy man.

choices.label: "Amala man in a Benz? Noted 😂"
choices.receipt: You noted his amala confession.

outcomes.text: 'Don't tell my guys.' He sends a picture of ewedu like it's a love letter.

choices.label: "Ikoyi is fine by me, sha."
choices.receipt: You told him Ikoyi was fine by you.

outcomes.text: 'Ikoyi it is, then.' He sounds slightly disappointed.

choices.label: "Send ₦20k, let me buy you some."
choices.receipt: You asked him to send amala money.

outcomes.text: ₦20k lands. 'Buy two wraps. One is yours.'

beats.text: If I ever disappear when there's wahala, don't take it personal. Meet me at the filling station on Ozumba Mbadiwe. Always. Okay?

choices.label: "Filling station. Got it. But why?"
choices.receipt: You noted his filling-station plan.

outcomes.text: 'Just in case.' Two words, and he goes offline.

choices.label: "Disappear?? Who are you running from?"
choices.receipt: You asked who he's running from.

outcomes.text: He sends a laughing emoji and nothing else. Loud.

choices.label: "You're so dramatic. Goodnight 😂"
choices.receipt: You called him dramatic and said goodnight.

outcomes.text: 'Goodnight, my peace.' Then he's typing for ten minutes. Nothing arrives.

beats.text: Phone is dying. If you ever can't reach me, call my cousin Tunde. He always knows where I am. Always.

choices.label: "Cousin Tunde. Saved. 📱"
choices.receipt: You saved his cousin Tunde's number.

outcomes.text: 'You're organised. I like that.' He sends Tunde's number twice.

choices.label: "Charge your phone like an adult."
choices.receipt: You told him to charge his phone.

outcomes.text: 'Yes, boss.' He sends a selfie with a power bank like a trophy.

choices.label: "Send airtime so I can call you."
choices.receipt: You asked him for airtime.

outcomes.text: ₦5k airtime. 'Call me, not Tunde.'

beats.text: Don't laugh, but I'm watching that new Nollywood film tonight. The one with the mother. I'm not crying. The AC is just strong.

choices.label: "The AC. Of course 😭 Save it for us."
choices.receipt: You promised to watch his Nollywood film with him.

outcomes.text: 'Don't tell anybody.' He sends a voice note sniffing. 'Allergies.'

choices.label: "Big Boy crying? I'm screenshotting this."
choices.receipt: You laughed at him for crying.

outcomes.text: 'Delete!' He sends ten crying-laughing emojis.

choices.label: "Send your Netflix password then."
choices.receipt: You asked for his streaming password.

outcomes.text: He sends it. It's '17Kayode17'. Of course it is.

beats.text: Sunday lunch at my dad's. Every Sunday, 1pm, no phones at the table. If I'm off, that's why. Don't vex.

choices.label: "Sunday at 1, no phones. Greet your dad."
choices.receipt: You noted his Sunday lunch with his dad.

outcomes.text: 'He'd like you. That's the scary part.'

choices.label: "Can I come to Sunday lunch?"
choices.receipt: You asked to come to Sunday lunch.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes of typing. Then: 'Soon. 😅'

choices.label: "Okay. Bring me jollof."
choices.receipt: You asked him to bring back jollof.

outcomes.text: 'If there's any left. My dad eats like a judge.'

beats.text: Today is my mum's remembrance. White lilies, every year. I don't really talk about it. Just... be gentle with me today.

choices.label: "White lilies. I'm here. Talk when you're ready."
choices.receipt: You were gentle on his mum's remembrance day.

outcomes.text: He doesn't reply for an hour. Then: 'Thank you.' Just that.

choices.label: "Sending hugs 🤗"
choices.receipt: You sent him hugs.

outcomes.text: He sends a heart. A small one.

choices.label: "Let's go out tonight. Distract you."
choices.receipt: You invited him out on his mum's remembrance.

outcomes.text: 'Maybe.' He doesn't come. You go anyway.
